correctness.rationale: Exact five-state elimination gives the published scalar \(F_B\). The primary-infection term is strictly decreasing in infected prevalence and increasing in primary transmission. A negative-real-root argument for the cleared cubic rules out a third positive equilibrium. Smooth rescaling \(I=B^{-1/2}y\), \(\beta=\beta_\infty+B^{-1/2}z\) has a unique nondegenerate critical maximum at \(y_0=\sqrt{\delta\mu/L}\), \(z_0=2\sqrt{\delta\mu L}/c\); uniform localization of all near-critical nonnegative scalar values eliminates remote folds. Separate implicit-function calculations yield the two endemic-branch expansions. Rational exact checks reproduce test signs and constants; no stability beyond equilibria is asserted.

originality.rationale: Khan et al. prove finite-reinfection backward-bifurcation existence and numerically compute \(\mathcal R_0^C\), but the inspected equations, Figure 6, §§5,7,8, and accessible Appendix B.1 did not provide the positive \(B\to\infty\) floor, explicit inverse-square-root correction, or the simultaneous \(B^{-1}\) versus order-one equilibrium scales. Earlier SEIRE and SVEIRE models establish reinfection backward bifurcation in nonidentical flows. A distinct earlier SEIRV result on local reinfection thresholds does not imply this singular global-fold asymptotic. Incomplete full-document comparison and unindexed literature remain residual risks.
residual_risks: Full downloadable PDF of the motivating paper and some related PDFs were unavailable; a repository advertised a lawful copy but access failed, while indexed publisher scientific sections were readable. The older SEIRE preprint was read in a full-text HTML rendering with some missing mathematical glyphs.
Unindexed or later mathematical literature may independently contain equivalent large-reinfection singular asymptotics.
Different epidemic mechanisms can possess similar square-root laws; this result asserts only the model-specific coefficients and equilibrium scaling.

value.rationale: The motivating source computes a numerical decline of the subcritical equilibrium-existence threshold as reinfection increases but does not determine whether it bottoms out at zero or a positive level, or the rate. The sharp positive limit \(1-\delta/K\), explicit \(B^{-1/2}\) fold correction, and distinct \(B^{-1}\) versus nonzero endemic branches close a motivated large-reinfection regime rather than recomputing a table or renaming a generic fold theorem.
